phyllotaxis.name: Helianthus annuus
phyllotaxis.credit: File:Sunflower Spiral.jpg, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0
phyllotaxis.finding: 621 florets segmented on a real seed head; cell circularity 0.79 against 0.85 for the golden-angle model, with parastichy counts checked against Swinton et al. 2016.

branching.name: Ginkgo biloba
branching.credit: File:Ginkgo biloba 01 SR 87-36-02 A.jpg, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
branching.finding: Runions space-colonisation veins with Murray's law at the junctions, measured on a real leaf; Ginkgo's open dichotomous veins form no loops, a reticulate leaf supplies the looped case.

wing.name: Odonata
wing.finding: Median wing-cell length stays at 0.78–0.99 mm across 150 million years and a sixfold range of wing length: the inhibition length is approximately, not strictly, conserved.
wing.credit: File:Orthetrum cancellatum.jpg, Tim Bekaert, Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

turing.name: Pomacanthus imperator
turing.credit: Diego Delso, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
turing.finding: Stripe spacing measured on a real flank (CV 0.15, 22 Y-junctions) against a Turing labyrinth and an equal-diffusion control that makes no pattern.

turing.name: Equus caballus
turing.credit: File:Palatum horse.JPG, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
turing.finding: An FGF/SHH Turing sheet raises 9 ridges on the Shh stripes; their duty cycle (0.42) is close to the segmented rugae (0.44–0.49), and the ridges vanish with equal diffusion.

turing.name: Bos taurus
turing.credit: Province of Ontario Picture Bureau, c.1920, Wikimedia Commons, public domain
turing.finding: Tested negative. On 10 cows a single-wavelength Turing pattern is rejected (it predicts ~125 uniform spots, the cows carry a few body-scale patches).

spiral.name: Nautilus pompilius
spiral.credit: File:Pu - Nautilus pompilius - 10.jpg, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
spiral.finding: The shell outline fits a logarithmic spiral (log-polar r ≈ 0.96), with synthetic-recovery and shuffle controls.

spiral.name: Ovis ammon
spiral.finding: A real horn gives a spiral angle of 74.7° (73.6–75.6), matching Thompson's 75°, but the angle moves to 87° when the tip arc is dropped. Verdict mixed.

spiral.name: Fusulinida
spiral.finding: A thin section gives a whorl ratio of 1.49 ± 0.10, matching Thompson's 1.5 and Triticites' 1.53; the late-whorl drift fails in some genera. Verdict mixed.
